_about: Deep check of the selected gold-set candidates against the corpus (chunks.jsonl, index 5d82173e1a7e). One entry per candidate id in data/eval/faq_candidates_all.csv. expected = chunk_ids that hold the answer (citations are built from these). check: verified = answer fully in these chunks; partial = only part is, reference trimmed to that part; inference = answer follows from the text but is not stated in it; corrected = source answer wrong or outdated, reference rewritten from the statute; excluded = dropped after checking. reference = null means use the source answer (answer_en) as it is. Checked by Claude 2026-10-10; to be confirmed by the author.

RDT-005.reference: The rules depend on where you work: the Employment Act 1955 applies in Peninsular Malaysia and the Labour Ordinances in Sabah and Sarawak. Under each, either party may end a contract of service by notice, or without notice by paying the other party an indemnity equal to the wages for the notice period (EA ss. 12-13; Sabah ss. 11-12; Sarawak ss. 12-13). An employer may dismiss an employee without notice for misconduct only after due inquiry (EA s.14(1); Sabah s.13(1); Sarawak s.14(1)). A workman who considers he was dismissed without just cause or excuse may make written representations to the Director General of Industrial Relations to be reinstated, within sixty days of the dismissal (Industrial Relations Act 1967, s.20(1) and (1A)). The statutes do not deal with an employer asking a dismissed employee to sign a resignation letter.
RDT-005.notes: Reference answer drafted by Claude from the statute text (forum posts have no reliable answer); author to confirm. No region: tests multiple_jurisdictions.

RDT-006.reference: An employer who fails to pay wages as required is deemed to have broken the contract of service (EA s.15(1); Sabah s.13A(1); Sarawak s.14A(1)). Either party may terminate a contract of service without notice in the event of a wilful breach of a condition of the contract by the other party (EA s.13(2); Sabah s.12(2); Sarawak s.13(2)); terminating on that ground does not require notice.
RDT-006.notes: Reference answer drafted by Claude from the statute text (forum posts have no reliable answer); author to confirm. That no indemnity is owed follows from s.13(2) ('without notice') but is not stated outright. No region.

RDT-007.reference: A contract of service for a period exceeding one month must be in writing (EA s.10(1)). Either party may end a contract of service by notice; where the contract has no written notice term, the notice must be at least four weeks if the employee has been employed for less than two years (EA s.12(2); Sabah s.11(2); Sarawak s.12(2)). A workman who considers he was dismissed without just cause or excuse may make written representations to be reinstated within sixty days of the dismissal (Industrial Relations Act 1967, s.20(1) and (1A)).
RDT-007.notes: Reference answer drafted by Claude from the statute text (forum posts have no reliable answer); author to confirm. Whether 'poor performance' is just cause is decided by the Industrial Court (case law, not held). No region.

RDT-008.reference: The length of notice is set by the written contract of service and must be the same for both employer and employee (EA s.12(2); Sabah s.11(2); Sarawak s.12(2)). Either party may instead end the contract by paying the other an indemnity equal to the wages for the notice period (EA s.13(1)). Whether an additional penalty for leaving before the end of a fixed-term contract is enforceable is a question of contract law, which GetRight does not hold.
RDT-008.notes: Reference answer drafted by Claude from the statute text (forum posts have no reliable answer); author to confirm. Penalty clause depends on the Contracts Act 1950 (not held). No region.

RDT-010.reference: Overtime work must be paid at a rate not less than one and a half times the hourly rate of pay, irrespective of the basis on which the rate of pay is fixed (EA s.60A(3)(a); Sabah s.104(6); Sarawak s.105(6)); the statute sets no point after which a lower rate applies. Normal hours are limited to eight a day, a spread over of ten hours and forty-five hours a week (EA s.60A(1)). The Director General of Labour may inquire into and decide disputes over wages due under the contract or the Act (EA s.69(1)).
RDT-010.notes: Reference answer drafted by Claude from the statute text (forum posts have no reliable answer); author to confirm. The monthly overtime limit (104 hours) is in regulations not held. Sarawak s.105(6) is marked superseded although A1754 s.34 did not change it (see data issue). No region.
